[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Ball in Berland** [CF 1475C · Ball in Berland](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1475/C){rating="1400"}

Counting good pairs of couples directly means checking two conditions; counting the **bad** ones means counting pairs that share a boy, plus pairs that share a girl. Two couples share boy $x$ in $\binom{\deg x}{2}$ ways, so the pairs sharing *some* boy number $\sum_x \binom{\deg_A x}{2}$, and likewise for girls. The two bad events could overlap only for two couples sharing both people — the same couple twice, which distinctness forbids. Inclusion–exclusion therefore has nothing to add back:
$$\text{answer} = \binom{k}{2} - \sum_{\text{boys } x} \binom{\deg_A x}{2} - \sum_{\text{girls } y} \binom{\deg_B y}{2}.$$
On the sample, boy $1$ and girl $2$ each have degree $2$, so the answer is $\binom{4}{2} - 1 - 1 = 4$.

[Solved in full in @sec-cnt-pcomp-ball.]{.card-link}
